previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 34-year-old woman was admitted after reporting a self-aborted suicide attempt involving accelerating her car without veering off the road. She endorsed passive suicidal ideation and feelings of being a burden to her family. During her 10-day psychiatric admission, she continued her weekly bilateral ECT sessions on days 3, 6, and 10, with gradual improvement in mood and reduction in suicidal thoughts. Her chronic conditions—hypothyroidism, endometriosis-related pain, asthma, and GERD—were monitored and managed with stable medications. She engaged in care, expressed connection to her infant child as a protective factor, and demonstrated improved emotional stability. She was discharged to an inpatient psychiatric facility for ongoing ECT and therapy, alert, cooperative, and with a reinforced safety plan.
